This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.8`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useSpyOn`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`test`](/linter/domains#test)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`jest/prefer-spy-on`](https://github.com/jest-community/eslint-plugin-jest/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-spy-on.md)
  - Same as [`vitest/prefer-spy-on`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/eslint-plugin-vitest/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-spy-on.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useSpyOn": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Enforce using `jest.spyOn()` or `vi.spyOn()` instead of overwriting a property with a mock function.

When a property is replaced with `jest.fn()` or `vi.fn()`, the original value is lost.
It has to be saved and put back by hand after the test, otherwise the mock leaks into
other tests. A mock created with `jest.spyOn()` or `vi.spyOn()` remembers the original
value, so it can be restored with `mockRestore()`, `restoreAllMocks()`, or the
`restoreMocks` setting of the test runner.

A spy calls the original function until you give it another implementation, for example
with `mockImplementation()` or `mockReturnValue()`.

The fix is unsafe because `spyOn()` throws an error when the property doesn't exist or
isn't a function, while the assignment always succeeds.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
Date.now = jest.fn();
```
